{"number":46,"title":"Spec: tutor v1 — MTG deckbuilding plugin for Claude Code","body":"## Problem Statement

The owner keeps a physical Magic: The Gathering collection — several hundred cards scanned into ManaBox — and plays Commander and casual formats at a family table. Building a new deck from that collection is slow and unreliable:

- Deck ideas drift into cards the owner does not own, and catching that means checking the list row by row against the app.
- Format rules — deck size, copy limits, color identity, banlists, Commander brackets — each need hand-checking, and a missed one surfaces mid-game.
- Copies already sitting in a built deck get double-counted into new lists, but one physical card cannot sit in two decks.
- Preparing several decks for one sitting (an Archenemy night, a Commander pod, teaching decks for the kids) multiplies all of the above and adds power-balance guesswork.
- Generic deckbuilding tools assume cards can be bought; the owner builds strictly from what is owned.

The owner wants deckbuilding to work the way their software work does: settle intent first, generate the checks, build until green, then get an honest review — from a phone or a desktop, with artifacts that round-trip into ManaBox.

## Solution

**tutor** — a Claude Code plugin, shipped from this repo, which doubles as its own plugin marketplace. Its skills mirror the `/implement` + `/code-review` software loop, applied to decks:

- **`/tutor:brief`** — a human-in-the-loop conversation that settles the Brief: Format, identity, Power, constraints, Donor Decks, and any play-variant asks. Ends with a Brief Block.
- **`/tutor:build`** — an autonomous, TDD-style loop. At start it generates the Suite — every deterministic Check the Deck must pass — from the Brief and the Format profile, before any card is picked. Counting Checks start red on the empty Deck; Build adds and swaps owned cards until the Suite is green (or ends red with an honest report). Ends with a ManaBox-importable Deck Block and the Suite's red/green report.
- **`/tutor:review`** — autonomous judgment of a finished Deck along two axes, Standards and Brief, delivered as severity-tagged Findings with mechanically computed Verdicts. Ends with a Review Block.
- **`/tutor:oracle`** — a utility outside the deck loop: generates the Oracle, the Scryfall-derived card-facts file covering the Collection, which Checks run against.

State lives as files in the **Collection home** — the working directory a tutor session runs in, holding the Export (`collection.csv`), the Oracle (`oracle.jsonl`), and built Blocks. For the owner that folder is a private git repo doubling as a deck library, reachable from the phone through the Claude Code mobile app; tutor itself sees only well-known filenames. A pasted Export or Block is always accepted and beats the file on conflict.

Multi-deck sittings are **Tables**: one brief conversation produces a Table Brief plus per-Deck Briefs; Seats build sequentially with contention resolved by seat order; a Table Review judges the finished sitting.

## User Stories

1. As a Claude Code user, I want to install tutor with `/plugin marketplace add mattiasthalen/tutor` followed by `/plugin install tutor@tutor`, so that setup is two commands with no manual file copying.
2. As a plugin user, I want every tutor command namespaced `/tutor:*`, so that it never collides with other plugins.
3. As the owner, I want tutor to run entirely inside Claude Code sessions — desktop, web, and the mobile app — so that I can build decks from my phone.
4. As the owner, I want the README to document the update path (enable auto-update for the marketplace, or `/plugin marketplace update` then `/plugin update tutor`), so that I know how releases reach me.
5. As the collection owner, I want to drop my ManaBox Export into the Collection home and have every tutor session read it from there, so that I never re-paste my collection.
6. As the collection owner, I want a pasted Export, Deck Block, or any other Block to always be accepted and to beat the file on conflict, so that the freshest thing in my hand wins.
7. As the collection owner, I want the Export parsed tolerantly — header-keyed, quoting-aware, malformed rows skipped and reported with examples — so that one odd row never sinks a build.
8. As the collection owner, I want my existing ManaBox decks recognized from the Export's deck rows, so that tutor knows which copies are already spoken for.
9. As a deckbuilder, I want copies in existing Decks committed by default, freed only when my Brief names them as Donor Decks, so that a new deck never silently cannibalizes one I still play.
10. As a deckbuilder, I want to free the whole Collection at once ("the entire collection is available"), so that a rebuild-everything mood needs one sentence, not a deck list.
11. As a deckbuilder, I want Build to report the contention it declined ("wanted Rhystic Study; all copies committed to Tatyova"), so that I can re-brief deliberately instead of wondering.
12. As the collection owner, I want the brief conversation to surface the Export's newest Added timestamp and ask once whether it is current, so that staleness is caught where a human can fix it.
13. As a deckbuilder, I want `/tutor:oracle` to build the card-facts file from my Export via Scryfall, so that Checks run on real card data instead of model memory.
14. As a deckbuilder, I want the Oracle trimmed to what Checks need — name-keyed, four sanctioned Formats' legalities, the Game Changer flag, no UUIDs — so that it stays small enough to load whole.
15. As a deckbuilder, I want a Deck card missing from the Oracle to degrade per-card to flagged model knowledge, never a hard failure, so that an incomplete Oracle still builds a deck honestly.
16. As a deckbuilder, I want Build to offer Oracle generation when the file is absent and network allows, so that the happy path assembles itself.
17. As the collection owner, I want Oracle freshness (its generation date and source-Export watermark, with a ~30-day drift nudge) folded into the brief's single freshness question, so that upkeep is one question, not a chore.
18. As a deckbuilder, I want a brief conversation that pins Format, identity, Power, and constraints before any card is picked, so that intent is settled first and drives everything downstream.
19. As a deckbuilder, I want the Brief captured as a flat `key: value` Block with only `format` required, so that a brief is quick to state and cheap to reuse.
20. As a deckbuilder, I want Power declared on a shared 1–5 ladder — read as official WotC Brackets in Commander, profile-interpreted in the 60-card Formats, defaulting to 2 — so that power talk is comparable across Formats.
21. As a deckbuilder, I want mechanical Brief asks ("must include X", "nothing above 5 mana") to become Checks and fuzzy asks ("feel like dragon tribal") to go to Review, so that every constraint lands where it can be honestly enforced.
22. As a deckbuilder, I want the Suite generated from Brief and Format profile before any card is picked, with every size, mana-base, curve, and quota Check red on the empty Deck, so that building is test-first, not test-after.
23. As a deckbuilder, I want every Check deterministic and binary — same Deck, same card facts, same verdict — so that green is trustworthy and two runs diff cleanly.
24. As a deckbuilder, I want Check classes covering Legality, Availability, Mana base, Curve, Role Quotas, mechanical Brief constraints, and hypergeometric Consistency where the profile sets a threshold, so that the deck's mechanics are covered end to end.
25. As a deckbuilder, I want Check targets to come from the Format profile with only my Brief allowed to override them, so that Build never silently bends a target to get green.
26. As a deckbuilder, I want the Suite to be a declarative file interpreted by a fixed, stdlib-only runner, so that an Upgrade re-runs the byte-identical artifact and nothing regenerates code.
27. As a deckbuilder, I want the red/green report to name each Check with its evidence and the cards involved, so that I can read exactly why a Check is red.
28. As a deckbuilder, I want Build allowed to end red with an honest report and my options (loosen the Brief, accept the Deck as-is, acquire cards), so that impossibility is surfaced rather than painted green.
29. As a deckbuilder, I want each nonbasic in the Deck Block pinned to the exact owned printing, with the fancier owned print chosen when I have several, so that physical assembly matches the list card for card.
30. As the owner, I want the Deck Block to be text ManaBox actually imports, so that a shipped deck goes straight into the app.
31. As the owner, I want the Maybeboard as a wishlist Board where unowned upgrade candidates live, so that the collection-only rule holds while good ideas are kept.
32. As a deckbuilder, I want Review split into a Standards axis (deckbuilding craft against a Smell baseline plus per-Format standards) and a Brief axis (fidelity to my stated intent), so that craft and intent are judged separately, like a code review.
33. As a deckbuilder, I want every Finding severity-tagged (blocker or note), naming its cards, with at most one suggestion — an owned swap or an unowned Maybeboard candidate — so that findings are actionable.
34. As a deckbuilder, I want at most five Findings per axis, worst first, with a one-line summary of the rest, so that a Review stays readable on a phone.
35. As a deckbuilder, I want Verdicts computed mechanically — any blocker means rebuild, only notes means playable, clean means ship, overall is the worst axis — so that no fresh judgment sneaks into aggregation.
36. As a deckbuilder, I want Review to trust the green Suite but still be able to flag a Check target as mis-set for my Brief ("24 lands passed, but this curve wants 26"), so that wrongly set targets get caught.
37. As the owner, I want any ManaBox deck reviewable without a Brief, with the Brief axis reporting "no Brief available", so that decks tutor did not build still get a Standards review.
38. As a deckbuilder, I want the Review's closing instructions to depend on the Verdict — ship suggests the ManaBox import, playable and rebuild offer a Build re-run that consumes the Review Block — so that the next step is always in front of me.
39. As a deckbuilder, I want an Upgrade to be an ordinary Build re-run with a fresh Export and the existing Deck (its own copies freed), so that improving a deck needs no fourth verb.
40. As a deckbuilder, I want the revision loop manual — I read the Review, then re-run Build with it as input — so that taste calls stay mine.
41. As the owner, I want every Block recognized by its shape alone, with no sentinels or version markers, so that a mangled or partial paste degrades gracefully instead of falling off a format cliff.
42. As a table host, I want one brief conversation for a whole Table that produces a Table Brief plus untouched per-Deck Briefs, so that a sitting is planned in one place.
43. As a table host, I want Seats built sequentially in seat order, with an earlier Seat's finished Deck counting as committed copies, so that one physical copy never sits in two decks at the same sitting.
44. As a table host, I want declared-Power match checked mechanically (every Seat's effective Power equals the table's unless its seat line overrides) and felt fairness judged in the Table Review, so that balance claims and balance reality are each handled where they belong.
45. As a table host, I want a Table Review after the last Seat — power spread, clashing play patterns, contention fallout — so that the sitting is judged as a whole, not just deck by deck.
46. As a parent, I want Kitchen 20 Packs built to the Foundations Beginner Box shape and judged on how well they combine, so that any two Packs shuffle into a fair 40-card teaching game.
47. As a deckbuilder, I want Commander, Kitchen 20, Casual 60, and thin Standard/Modern/Pioneer profiles as equal citizens, so that my actual play — from kitchen table to store-legal — is all covered.
48. As a deckbuilder, I want play variants (Archenemy, Two-Headed Giant, Jumpstart 40) expressed in the Brief rather than as Formats, so that a table setup shapes intent without multiplying rulebooks.
49. As the maintainer, I want adding a Format later to be a new data profile, not engine work, so that house formats stay cheap.
50. As the maintainer, I want one pinned semver as the sole version authority, a release to be the deliberate bump commit performed by a release script, and every release tagged, so that users update predictably and docs churn ships nothing.
51. As the maintainer, I want structural plugin validation running in CI from day one, so that a broken manifest never reaches an install.
52. As the maintainer, I want Evals — deterministic, offline, fixture-driven — that judge tutor itself, so that skill changes are testable without touching the live Scryfall API.
53. As a user, I want the WotC Fan Content and Scryfall notices visible where the policy expects them, so that the project stays compliant and unmistakably unofficial.

## Implementation Decisions

Vocabulary throughout is the glossary in `CONTEXT.md` (Collection, Export, Collection home, Brief, Deck, Review, Finding, Verdict, Smell, Block, Board, Maybeboard, Upgrade, Donor Deck, Format, Play variant, Centerpiece, Kitchen 20, Pack, Check, Suite, Role, Oracle, Eval, Table, Power, Seat, Table Brief, Table Review). ADRs 0001–0007 bind; ADR 0007 (Claude Code only, Collection home) is the current runtime baseline.

### Plugin and marketplace

- One repo is both the plugin and its marketplace: plugin manifest and marketplace catalog side by side, the single marketplace entry pointing back at the repo root. Skills live one folder per skill; commands are namespaced `/tutor:*` and are thin wrappers over the skills (ADR 0001).
- Install: `/plugin marketplace add mattiasthalen/tutor`, then `/plugin install tutor@tutor`.
- Claude Code is the only runtime (ADR 0007): skills may rely on session affordances — working-directory files, network access, subagents. Portable-skill authoring survives as a style discipline, not a contract.

### State: the Collection home

- The working directory holds `collection.csv` (the Export), `oracle.jsonl` (the Oracle), and built Blocks (convention: a `decks/` folder). Well-known filenames are the mechanism; git-ness is invisible to skills. The documented recommendation for the owner is a private collection repo doubling as a deck library, reachable from the phone.
- A pasted Export or Block is always legal input and beats the file on conflict; the session reports the diff so drift is visible. A pasted Deck Block beats the Export's deck rows.

### Workflow

- Three-stage loop: brief (HITL) → build (autonomous) → review (autonomous), chaining via each skill's closing instructions; every stage independently invocable. `oracle` sits outside the loop as maintenance.
- Upgrade is a Build re-run with a fresh Export and the existing Deck; the rebuilt Deck's own copies are freed automatically. No fourth deck verb exists.
- The revision loop is manual: the human reads the Review, then re-runs Build with the Review Block as input. No automatic review→build loop.
- The review command fans out two parallel subagents, one per axis, aggregated side by side without merging or reranking; a sequential two-pass fallback stays as robustness (ADR 0006 as amended).

### Collection ingestion

- The raw whole CSV is read in-session; no derived digest artifact. Parsing is tolerant, header-keyed (never positional), RFC-4180-aware, UTF-8 with BOM tolerance; malformed rows are skipped and reported with a count and examples; the only hard failure is a header missing the identity columns.
- Row identity: Scryfall ID first, Name + Set code fallback. Columns consumed: Binder Name, Binder Type, Name, Set code, Collector number, Quantity, Foil, Scryfall ID, Added. Everything else is ignored; Purchase price is acquisition cost, never a live price.
- Deck recognition: rows with `Binder Type` of `deck` belong to the Deck named by `Binder Name`.
- Contention: deck-row copies are committed by default. The Brief frees them via `donor:` lines (repeatable, value an existing Deck name; `donor: all` frees everything); an Upgrade frees the target Deck's own rows. Build reports contention it declined.
- Freshness: the brief asks once, using the newest `Added` timestamp (plus the Oracle's staleness signals); downstream stages trust their input silently.
- Condition, Language, and Foil vocabularies are treated as open behind defensive normalization (confirmed values are snake_case; Chinese language codes and `etched` remain unverified).

### Formats

- v1 Formats, all equal citizens: **Commander**, **Kitchen 20**, **Casual 60**, and thin sanctioned **Standard / Modern / Pioneer** (legality read from the Oracle's per-card legalities; no hand-maintained banlists). The four 60-card Formats share one set of review standards.
- A Format is a first-class data profile: deck size, copy limits, color rules, banlist parameters, check targets (lands, curve shape, quota numbers, consistency thresholds), per-Format review standards, and judgment-flavored lists such as which keywords count as evergreen. A later format is a new profile, not engine work.
- Kitchen 20 profile (pinned by the Foundations Beginner Box research): 20-card mono-color Pack, strict singleton nonlands, 8–9 lands with Uncharted Haven the only nonbasic, exactly 1 rare, evergreen keywords only, no multicolor cards; two Packs shuffle into a 40-card game (~16–18 lands); pack-combining quality is review guidance; the Format carries no Power.
- Play variants (Archenemy, Two-Headed Giant, Jumpstart 40) shape the Brief; the Deck is always built to some Format. The Centerpiece unifies the commander and the Archenemy villain's planeswalker.

### Blocks

- Recognition is semantic — no sentinel lines, no fence-tag reliance, no version markers. Shape alone identifies each Block; partial pastes degrade gracefully. Blocks are atomic: nothing embeds another Block. Closing instructions name which Blocks the next stage needs.
- **Deck Block** — ManaBox-importable text (owner-verified: ManaBox accepts `//` comments and reserves the four Board headers). First line `// `; Board headers `// Commander`, `// Mainboard`, `// Sideboard`, `// Maybeboard`, only the Boards the Format uses; nonbasics as pinned English lines with set code and collector number (fancier owned print wins), optional inline `// category` comments; basics lumped per name, last in each Board after a blank line; Maybeboard entries may be unowned and carry no printing pin. From the Block-formats decision:

  ```
  // Golgari Reanimator

  // Commander
  1 Meren of Clan Nel Toth (C15) 49

  // Mainboard
  1 Sol Ring (C21) 263 // ramp
  1 Eternal Witness (MH2) 302 // recursion

  12 Forest
  8 Swamp

  // Maybeboard
  1 Mikaeus, the Unhallowed // would make the deck imba
  ```

- **Brief Block** — flat `key: value` lines. Canonical keys: `name`, `format`, `centerpiece`, `identity`, `play variant`, `power`, `constraint` (repeatable), `donor` (repeatable; `donor: all` frees the whole Collection), `notes`. Only `format` is required. There is no `budget:` key.
- **Review Block** — `deck:` and `date:` reference lines, one overall `verdict:` line, then one section per axis (Standards, Brief) with its own verdict and Findings naming cards.
- **Suite report Block** — flat `suite:`/`deck:`/`format:`/`date:`/`oracle:` head, one `verdict:` line, then one `red|green  — evidence` line per Check, findings naming cards (shape from the suite prototype).
- **Table Brief Block** — same flat grammar, recognized by its `table:` anchor plus `seat:` lines; an index that never embeds the per-Deck Briefs. Seat grammar `seat: [role —] [, power N]`; the deck name joins to that Brief's `name:`. From the Tables decision:

  ```
  table: Family Archenemy Night
  format: commander
  play variant: archenemy
  power: 3
  seat: villain — Nicol Bolas, God-Pharaoh, power 4
  seat: hero — Meren Reanimator
  ```

- **Table Review Block** — `table:`/`date:` lines, one overall `verdict:`, per-axis sections whose findings name Seats and cards.

### Checks and the Suite

- A deck test is a Suite of deterministic, binary Checks generated test-first from Brief + Format profile at Build start (ADR 0003). Check classes: Legality (Format-parameterized, including Kitchen 20's packet rules and the Commander bracket's Game Changers count), Availability (owned copies, contention-aware), Mana base, Curve, Quotas (counts over Role tags), mechanical Brief constraints, and hypergeometric Consistency where the profile sets a threshold. No budget class.
- Empty-Deck semantics (ADR 0005 amending 0003): every size, mana-base, curve, and quota Check starts red; constraint-shaped Checks (singleton, legality lists, availability) may pass vacuously. Vacuous green is honest.
- Verdicts are strictly binary — no warn tier. Build may end red with an honest report; the human decides among loosening the Brief, accepting as-is, or acquiring cards.
- The Suite is declarative data interpreted by a fixed runner (ADR 0005): sections for profile targets (snapshotted at generation), quotas, mechanical constraints, and Role tags (judgment recorded once per card), plus check ids resolving to fixed predicates. The runner is a stdlib-only skill asset with its own small YAML-subset parser; the same data renders as a walkable checklist, flagged best-effort, where no sandbox exists. An Upgrade re-runs the byte-identical Suite; only cards new to the pool need fresh tagging. Portability was proven with two independent interpreters (Python and JavaScript) agreeing on every verdict — from the prototype, which is the reference implementation.
- The global Role vocabulary: ramp, draw, removal, wipe, wincon, land, theme/other. A card may carry several Roles and counts toward each; tagging is judgment, counting is mechanical.
- The Game Changers Check reads the Oracle's `game_changer` flag; bracket limits (0 / 0 / ≤3 / unlimited / unlimited for Power 1–5) are Format-profile data.

### Review

- Two axes, mirroring `/code-review` (ADR 0006): **Standards** — a format-agnostic Smell baseline plus per-Format standards, where the profile overrides the baseline — and **Brief** — fidelity to intent. No third axis.
- Smell baseline v1 (names locked, wording polished at implementation): synergy island, dead card, win-more, no comeback plan, piloting overload, fragile mana, theme tax, redundancy gap, curve lie, interaction mismatch.
- Per-Format standards are authored at implementation from recorded seeds: Kitchen 20 — Pack-combining quality, teaching pilotability, rare-as-payoff; Commander — politics, functional-copy redundancy, answer spread; one shared list for the four 60-card Formats. Power fit ("does it play like its number"), mass land denial, chained extra turns, and early two-card combos are Review judgment, not Checks.
- A Finding: severity (blocker / note) + named cards + the problem + at most one suggestion (owned swap or unowned Maybeboard candidate). Cap five per axis, worst first, plus a one-line summary of the rest. Review never edits the Deck.
- Verdicts are arithmetic: axis with any blocker → `rebuild`; only notes → `playable`; clean → `ship`; overall = worst axis. Review trusts the green Suite — it never recounts — but may flag a Check target as mis-set for the Brief.
- No Brief present: Standards-only review; the Brief axis reports "no Brief available". Closing instructions are Verdict-dependent (ship → ManaBox import suggestion; playable/rebuild → offer a Build re-run consuming the Review Block).

### The Oracle

- `/tutor:oracle` reads the Export, batch-resolves unique Scryfall IDs via Scryfall's collection endpoint (75 identifiers per call, 2 calls/second, mandatory User-Agent and Accept headers), falling back to Name + Set code for migrated or deleted IDs, and writes `oracle.jsonl` beside the Export. The bulk-file path was rejected (print-level IDs miss in the oracle-level bulk file; the download buys nothing at collection scale).
- Shape: one JSON line per unique card name — prints deduped, token rows excluded, basic lands included, multi-faced cards flattened with `//`. Fields: name, mana value, colors, color identity, type line, oracle text, legalities trimmed to standard/pioneer/modern/commander, and the `game_changer` boolean. No UUIDs.
- Line one records `generated_at` plus the source Export's newest `Added`. Two staleness signals — Export newer than the Oracle's watermark, or `generated_at` older than ~30 days — fold into the brief's single freshness question. No automation; regenerate when the Export refreshes or the nudge fires.
- A Deck card missing from the Oracle degrades per-card to flagged model knowledge; the Build report lists uncovered cards and recommends regeneration. When no Oracle exists and network allows, build offers to generate one on the spot.

### Tables

- One brief conversation per Table produces one Table Brief plus N untouched per-Deck Briefs (two Seats minimum). Table-level power, constraints, play variant, and donors copy into each Seat's Brief, so every build session reads only its own Brief.
- Seat order = build order = contention priority. Builds run sequentially through the unchanged build skill; a table-mate's finished Deck Block counts as committed copies. Table-mates are never Donor Decks; reallocation is a human loop — Table Review flags it, the owner re-briefs, affected Seats re-run in order.
- Table `power:` is inherited per Seat with per-seat override (e.g. villain above heroes); declared-power match is a mechanical Check, felt fairness is Table Review judgment. Kitchen 20 Seats carry no Power.
- One Format per Table; play variants ride on top. A Kitchen 20 Pack set built to combine is a Table like any other. Upgrading one Seat later is an ordinary Upgrade carrying the Table Brief and table-mate Deck Blocks.

### Constraint vocabulary

- `power:` is a number 1–5; free text may trail for feel ("3, battlecruiser feel") but the number is canonical. Commander reads it as the official WotC Bracket; the 60-card Formats profile-interpret it (1 jank … 5 competitive); absent defaults to 2; Kitchen 20 carries none.
- Proxies are out of scope by premise (collection-only; the Maybeboard is the valve). Budget is out entirely — no key, no price semantics.

### Versioning and release

- One release channel: the marketplace plugin (ADR 0004). One explicit semver pinned in the plugin manifest as sole version authority, mirrored into each skill's free-form metadata version — plugin and skills version in lockstep as one organism.
- A release is the deliberate version-bump commit, performed by a release script: bump, mirror into skills, draft the changelog entry (Keep a Changelog shape), run the plugin validator, tag `tutor--v{version}`, push. Unbumped merges deliberately ship nothing.
- Semver for prompt-ware: MAJOR = existing artifacts break (a Block format change an existing Block cannot survive through Upgrade, or a skill/command removed or renamed); MINOR = new capability (Format profile, skill, Check class); PATCH = prompt fixes, wording, docs inside skills.
- README documents the update path (auto-update off by default for self-hosted marketplaces). No stable/latest split; GitHub Releases deferred until the public phase.

### Legal

- tutor is unofficial Fan Content under the WotC Fan Content Policy. The mandated disclaimer ships verbatim: "tutor is unofficial Fan Content permitted under the Fan Content Policy. Not approved/endorsed by Wizards. Portions of the materials used are property of Wizards of the Coast. ©Wizards of the Coast LLC."
- Scryfall notices apply (tutor calls the Scryfall API in the oracle skill): no implied endorsement, price/legality data marked informational-only, artist/copyright credit preserved if card images are ever rendered.
- Placements: a Legal section in the README, a canonical NOTICE file at the repo root carrying the full composite text, the short form in the plugin and marketplace descriptions, and a short-form footer line on generated deck artifacts plus a price/legality caveat wherever those surface. The plugin stays free and unpaywalled — a condition of both policies.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test**: judge external behavior only. A skill is judged by the artifacts and transcript it produces — the Blocks emitted, the Checks run, the files written — never by its internal reasoning. A Check is judged by its verdict over a given Deck and Oracle. Planted flaws in fixtures make judgment measurable.
- **Seams** (existing ones, at the highest point; no new seams proposed): the **skill boundary** — files/Blocks in, files/Blocks out — is where Evals drive brief, build, review, and oracle end-to-end; and the **Suite runner** — the one deterministic code seam, running offline over Suite + Deck + Oracle files. Deck-test Checks are the single authority on deck correctness; Eval graders wrap the runner rather than re-implement legality logic.
- **Harness, staged**: the plugin validator's strict mode runs in CI on every PR from day one; the skill-creator eval workflow is the dev-time behavioral harness; the gated `claude plugin eval` becomes the CI behavioral gate when org enablement lands (cases authored in skill-creator format now, ported then — its grader vocabulary maps cleanly onto the loop).
- **Depth split**: deep behavioral Evals for build and review; smoke for brief (fires from natural language, valid Brief Block from scripted answers) and for oracle (against the pinned snapshot). Brief conversation quality stays human-judged.
- **Input modes**: file-on-disk is primary; one pasted-Export case remains as parser-tolerance smoke.
- **Graders, two tiers**: hard mechanical invariants — every Deck card drawn from the Collection fixture, Format legality, the Deck Block parses as ManaBox-importable text, Blocks survive the round-trip — any failure red; soft LLM judgment — the Deck honors the Brief's intent, the Review catches planted flaws. Baseline/ablation grading joins for regression once plugin eval is available.
- **Fixtures, four kinds**: the real captured export (577 rows, ManaBox 4.1.12) as the realism fixture; small synthetic Collections for what it lacks (etched foil, non-English languages, promo collector numbers, per-Format shaped pools); fixture Briefs and Decks, some with planted flaws; and a pinned Scryfall snapshot covering only fixture cards, committed beside them and refreshed deliberately. **Evals never call the live API** — runs stay deterministic and offline.
- **Prior art**: the suite-shape prototype — fixture Suite, two independent interpreters, three-stage captured runs (empty / planted-violations draft / green final) — is the model for Check-level testing; the skill-creator eval workflow is the model for skill-level Evals.

## Out of Scope

- **Building unowned-card decks, proxies, and budget reasoning** — tutor builds from the Collection; the Maybeboard is the only home for unowned cards; no price semantics anywhere.
- **The claude.ai chat runtime and skill-ZIP channel** — retired (ADR 0004, ADR 0007). Reviving chat is a fresh effort.
- **Goldfishing and turn simulation** — only closed-form hypergeometric math qualifies as a Check; whether any simulation ever joins Review is a later question.
- **Scheme decks** — fixed product, no construction choice; a Brief may note the villain's table role.
- **Mixed-Format Tables** — one Format per Table until a real sitting demands otherwise.
- **An automatic review→build loop** — the human reads the Review and re-runs Build; some findings are taste.
- **Automatic seat reallocation** — contention across a Table resolves through a human re-brief, never by unbuilding an earlier Seat.
- **Release channels, GitHub Releases, and public distribution** — one marketplace, one channel, main is it; the public phase ("the world next") is a later effort.
- **Collection compaction** — the raw CSV is read whole; revisit only near ~2,000 rows.
- **Card acquisition advice** — Build may state that acquiring cards is an option when ending red; recommending purchases is not tutor's job.

## Further Notes

- **Provenance**: this spec assembles the decisions of the wayfinder map [Wayfinder map: tutor — MTG deckbuilding plugin with its own marketplace](https://github.com/mattiasthalen/tutor/issues/2) — every closed child ticket's resolution comment is source material. ADRs 0001–0007 and the `CONTEXT.md` glossary are binding; where this spec and an ADR diverge, flag it rather than silently overriding.
- **Reference assets**: the suite-shape prototype (runnable Suite, two interpreters, captured runs, interactive demo) lives on branch `claude/deck-test-artifact-shape-wk1txl`; the real export sample and verification script on `claude/manabox-export-sample-irxrfp`; research write-ups on their `research/*` branches, linked from each research ticket.
- **Open verifications, parser posture only**: Chinese language codes and the `etched` foil value remain unobserved in a real export; both touch ignored or normalized columns, so they gate nothing — keep the vocabularies open behind defensive normalization.
- **Kitchen 20 life total** (20) is medium-confidence — the printed booklet was never inspected; nothing mechanical depends on it.
- **Plugin eval enablement** is org-gated and publicly undocumented; spike it at implementation time rather than blocking on it.
- **The deck library vision**: the owner's Collection home accumulates many built Decks and Tables — "generate MANY decks and tables… look it up and build the decks when I want." Skills should treat the `decks/` folder as a growing library, not a scratch directory.
- **Posture**: me first, the world next. The repo is private today; the legal wording is already public-ready; whether the real collection sample ships publicly parks with the release flow when the public phase arrives.

{"number":46,"title":"Spec: tutor v1 — MTG deckbuilding plugin for Claude Code","body":"## Problem Statement

The owner keeps a physical Magic: The Gathering collection — several hundred cards scanned into ManaBox — and plays Commander and casual formats at a family table. Building a new deck from that collection is slow and unreliable:

- Deck ideas drift into cards the owner does not own, and catching that means checking the list row by row against the app.
- Format rules — deck size, copy limits, color identity, banlists, Commander brackets — each need hand-checking, and a missed one surfaces mid-game.
- Copies already sitting in a built deck get double-counted into new lists, but one physical card cannot sit in two decks.
- Preparing several decks for one sitting (an Archenemy night, a Commander pod, teaching decks for the kids) multiplies all of the above and adds power-balance guesswork.
- Generic deckbuilding tools assume cards can be bought; the owner builds strictly from what is owned.

The owner wants deckbuilding to work the way their software work does: settle intent first, generate the checks, build until green, then get an honest review — from a phone or a desktop, with artifacts that round-trip into ManaBox.

## Solution

**tutor** — a Claude Code plugin, shipped from this repo, which doubles as its own plugin marketplace. Its skills mirror the `/implement` + `/code-review` software loop, applied to decks:

- **`/tutor:brief`** — a human-in-the-loop conversation that settles the Brief: Format, identity, Power, constraints, Donor Decks, and any play-variant asks. Ends with a Brief Block.
- **`/tutor:build`** — an autonomous, TDD-style loop. At start it generates the Suite — every deterministic Check the Deck must pass — from the Brief and the Format profile, before any card is picked. Counting Checks start red on the empty Deck; Build adds and swaps owned cards until the Suite is green (or ends red with an honest report). Ends with a ManaBox-importable Deck Block and the Suite's red/green report.
- **`/tutor:review`** — autonomous judgment of a finished Deck along two axes, Standards and Brief, delivered as severity-tagged Findings with mechanically computed Verdicts. Ends with a Review Block.
- **`/tutor:oracle`** — a utility outside the deck loop: generates the Oracle, the Scryfall-derived card-facts file covering the Collection, which Checks run against.

State lives as files in the **Collection home** — the working directory a tutor session runs in, holding the Export (`collection.csv`), the Oracle (`oracle.jsonl`), and built Blocks. For the owner that folder is a private git repo doubling as a deck library, reachable from the phone through the Claude Code mobile app; tutor itself sees only well-known filenames. A pasted Export or Block is always accepted and beats the file on conflict.

Multi-deck sittings are **Tables**: one brief conversation produces a Table Brief plus per-Deck Briefs; Seats build sequentially with contention resolved by seat order; a Table Review judges the finished sitting.

## User Stories

1. As a Claude Code user, I want to install tutor with `/plugin marketplace add mattiasthalen/tutor` followed by `/plugin install tutor@tutor`, so that setup is two commands with no manual file copying.
2. As a plugin user, I want every tutor command namespaced `/tutor:*`, so that it never collides with other plugins.
3. As the owner, I want tutor to run entirely inside Claude Code sessions — desktop, web, and the mobile app — so that I can build decks from my phone.
4. As the owner, I want the README to document the update path (enable auto-update for the marketplace, or `/plugin marketplace update` then `/plugin update tutor`), so that I know how releases reach me.
5. As the collection owner, I want to drop my ManaBox Export into the Collection home and have every tutor session read it from there, so that I never re-paste my collection.
6. As the collection owner, I want a pasted Export, Deck Block, or any other Block to always be accepted and to beat the file on conflict, so that the freshest thing in my hand wins.
7. As the collection owner, I want the Export parsed tolerantly — header-keyed, quoting-aware, malformed rows skipped and reported with examples — so that one odd row never sinks a build.
8. As the collection owner, I want my existing ManaBox decks recognized from the Export's deck rows, so that tutor knows which copies are already spoken for.
9. As a deckbuilder, I want copies in existing Decks committed by default, freed only when my Brief names them as Donor Decks, so that a new deck never silently cannibalizes one I still play.
10. As a deckbuilder, I want to free the whole Collection at once ("the entire collection is available"), so that a rebuild-everything mood needs one sentence, not a deck list.
11. As a deckbuilder, I want Build to report the contention it declined ("wanted Rhystic Study; all copies committed to Tatyova"), so that I can re-brief deliberately instead of wondering.
12. As the collection owner, I want the brief conversation to surface the Export's newest Added timestamp and ask once whether it is current, so that staleness is caught where a human can fix it.
13. As a deckbuilder, I want `/tutor:oracle` to build the card-facts file from my Export via Scryfall, so that Checks run on real card data instead of model memory.
14. As a deckbuilder, I want the Oracle trimmed to what Checks need — name-keyed, four sanctioned Formats' legalities, the Game Changer flag, no UUIDs — so that it stays small enough to load whole.
15. As a deckbuilder, I want a Deck card missing from the Oracle to degrade per-card to flagged model knowledge, never a hard failure, so that an incomplete Oracle still builds a deck honestly.
16. As a deckbuilder, I want Build to offer Oracle generation when the file is absent and network allows, so that the happy path assembles itself.
17. As the collection owner, I want Oracle freshness (its generation date and source-Export watermark, with a ~30-day drift nudge) folded into the brief's single freshness question, so that upkeep is one question, not a chore.
18. As a deckbuilder, I want a brief conversation that pins Format, identity, Power, and constraints before any card is picked, so that intent is settled first and drives everything downstream.
19. As a deckbuilder, I want the Brief captured as a flat `key: value` Block with only `format` required, so that a brief is quick to state and cheap to reuse.
20. As a deckbuilder, I want Power declared on a shared 1–5 ladder — read as official WotC Brackets in Commander, profile-interpreted in the 60-card Formats, defaulting to 2 — so that power talk is comparable across Formats.
21. As a deckbuilder, I want mechanical Brief asks ("must include X", "nothing above 5 mana") to become Checks and fuzzy asks ("feel like dragon tribal") to go to Review, so that every constraint lands where it can be honestly enforced.
22. As a deckbuilder, I want the Suite generated from Brief and Format profile before any card is picked, with every size, mana-base, curve, and quota Check red on the empty Deck, so that building is test-first, not test-after.
23. As a deckbuilder, I want every Check deterministic and binary — same Deck, same card facts, same verdict — so that green is trustworthy and two runs diff cleanly.
24. As a deckbuilder, I want Check classes covering Legality, Availability, Mana base, Curve, Role Quotas, mechanical Brief constraints, and hypergeometric Consistency where the profile sets a threshold, so that the deck's mechanics are covered end to end.
25. As a deckbuilder, I want Check targets to come from the Format profile with only my Brief allowed to override them, so that Build never silently bends a target to get green.
26. As a deckbuilder, I want the Suite to be a declarative file interpreted by a fixed, stdlib-only runner, so that an Upgrade re-runs the byte-identical artifact and nothing regenerates code.
27. As a deckbuilder, I want the red/green report to name each Check with its evidence and the cards involved, so that I can read exactly why a Check is red.
28. As a deckbuilder, I want Build allowed to end red with an honest report and my options (loosen the Brief, accept the Deck as-is, acquire cards), so that impossibility is surfaced rather than painted green.
29. As a deckbuilder, I want each nonbasic in the Deck Block pinned to the exact owned printing, with the fancier owned print chosen when I have several, so that physical assembly matches the list card for card.
30. As the owner, I want the Deck Block to be text ManaBox actually imports, so that a shipped deck goes straight into the app.
31. As the owner, I want the Maybeboard as a wishlist Board where unowned upgrade candidates live, so that the collection-only rule holds while good ideas are kept.
32. As a deckbuilder, I want Review split into a Standards axis (deckbuilding craft against a Smell baseline plus per-Format standards) and a Brief axis (fidelity to my stated intent), so that craft and intent are judged separately, like a code review.
33. As a deckbuilder, I want every Finding severity-tagged (blocker or note), naming its cards, with at most one suggestion — an owned swap or an unowned Maybeboard candidate — so that findings are actionable.
34. As a deckbuilder, I want at most five Findings per axis, worst first, with a one-line summary of the rest, so that a Review stays readable on a phone.
35. As a deckbuilder, I want Verdicts computed mechanically — any blocker means rebuild, only notes means playable, clean means ship, overall is the worst axis — so that no fresh judgment sneaks into aggregation.
36. As a deckbuilder, I want Review to trust the green Suite but still be able to flag a Check target as mis-set for my Brief ("24 lands passed, but this curve wants 26"), so that wrongly set targets get caught.
37. As the owner, I want any ManaBox deck reviewable without a Brief, with the Brief axis reporting "no Brief available", so that decks tutor did not build still get a Standards review.
38. As a deckbuilder, I want the Review's closing instructions to depend on the Verdict — ship suggests the ManaBox import, playable and rebuild offer a Build re-run that consumes the Review Block — so that the next step is always in front of me.
39. As a deckbuilder, I want an Upgrade to be an ordinary Build re-run with a fresh Export and the existing Deck (its own copies freed), so that improving a deck needs no fourth verb.
40. As a deckbuilder, I want the revision loop manual — I read the Review, then re-run Build with it as input — so that taste calls stay mine.
41. As the owner, I want every Block recognized by its shape alone, with no sentinels or version markers, so that a mangled or partial paste degrades gracefully instead of falling off a format cliff.
42. As a table host, I want one brief conversation for a whole Table that produces a Table Brief plus untouched per-Deck Briefs, so that a sitting is planned in one place.
43. As a table host, I want Seats built sequentially in seat order, with an earlier Seat's finished Deck counting as committed copies, so that one physical copy never sits in two decks at the same sitting.
44. As a table host, I want declared-Power match checked mechanically (every Seat's effective Power equals the table's unless its seat line overrides) and felt fairness judged in the Table Review, so that balance claims and balance reality are each handled where they belong.
45. As a table host, I want a Table Review after the last Seat — power spread, clashing play patterns, contention fallout — so that the sitting is judged as a whole, not just deck by deck.
46. As a parent, I want Kitchen 20 Packs built to the Foundations Beginner Box shape and judged on how well they combine, so that any two Packs shuffle into a fair 40-card teaching game.
47. As a deckbuilder, I want Commander, Kitchen 20, Casual 60, and thin Standard/Modern/Pioneer profiles as equal citizens, so that my actual play — from kitchen table to store-legal — is all covered.
48. As a deckbuilder, I want play variants (Archenemy, Two-Headed Giant, Jumpstart 40) expressed in the Brief rather than as Formats, so that a table setup shapes intent without multiplying rulebooks.
49. As the maintainer, I want adding a Format later to be a new data profile, not engine work, so that house formats stay cheap.
50. As the maintainer, I want one pinned semver as the sole version authority, a release to be the deliberate bump commit performed by a release script, and every release tagged, so that users update predictably and docs churn ships nothing.
51. As the maintainer, I want structural plugin validation running in CI from day one, so that a broken manifest never reaches an install.
52. As the maintainer, I want Evals — deterministic, offline, fixture-driven — that judge tutor itself, so that skill changes are testable without touching the live Scryfall API.
53. As a user, I want the WotC Fan Content and Scryfall notices visible where the policy expects them, so that the project stays compliant and unmistakably unofficial.

## Implementation Decisions

Vocabulary throughout is the glossary in `CONTEXT.md` (Collection, Export, Collection home, Brief, Deck, Review, Finding, Verdict, Smell, Block, Board, Maybeboard, Upgrade, Donor Deck, Format, Play variant, Centerpiece, Kitchen 20, Pack, Check, Suite, Role, Oracle, Eval, Table, Power, Seat, Table Brief, Table Review). ADRs 0001–0007 bind; ADR 0007 (Claude Code only, Collection home) is the current runtime baseline.

### Plugin and marketplace

- One repo is both the plugin and its marketplace: plugin manifest and marketplace catalog side by side, the single marketplace entry pointing back at the repo root. Skills live one folder per skill; commands are namespaced `/tutor:*` and are thin wrappers over the skills (ADR 0001).
- Install: `/plugin marketplace add mattiasthalen/tutor`, then `/plugin install tutor@tutor`.
- Claude Code is the only runtime (ADR 0007): skills may rely on session affordances — working-directory files, network access, subagents. Portable-skill authoring survives as a style discipline, not a contract.

### State: the Collection home

- The working directory holds `collection.csv` (the Export), `oracle.jsonl` (the Oracle), and built Blocks (convention: a `decks/` folder). Well-known filenames are the mechanism; git-ness is invisible to skills. The documented recommendation for the owner is a private collection repo doubling as a deck library, reachable from the phone.
- A pasted Export or Block is always legal input and beats the file on conflict; the session reports the diff so drift is visible. A pasted Deck Block beats the Export's deck rows.

### Workflow

- Three-stage loop: brief (HITL) → build (autonomous) → review (autonomous), chaining via each skill's closing instructions; every stage independently invocable. `oracle` sits outside the loop as maintenance.
- Upgrade is a Build re-run with a fresh Export and the existing Deck; the rebuilt Deck's own copies are freed automatically. No fourth deck verb exists.
- The revision loop is manual: the human reads the Review, then re-runs Build with the Review Block as input. No automatic review→build loop.
- The review command fans out two parallel subagents, one per axis, aggregated side by side without merging or reranking; a sequential two-pass fallback stays as robustness (ADR 0006 as amended).

### Collection ingestion

- The raw whole CSV is read in-session; no derived digest artifact. Parsing is tolerant, header-keyed (never positional), RFC-4180-aware, UTF-8 with BOM tolerance; malformed rows are skipped and reported with a count and examples; the only hard failure is a header missing the identity columns.
- Row identity: Scryfall ID first, Name + Set code fallback. Columns consumed: Binder Name, Binder Type, Name, Set code, Collector number, Quantity, Foil, Scryfall ID, Added. Everything else is ignored; Purchase price is acquisition cost, never a live price.
- Deck recognition: rows with `Binder Type` of `deck` belong to the Deck named by `Binder Name`.
- Contention: deck-row copies are committed by default. The Brief frees them via `donor:` lines (repeatable, value an existing Deck name; `donor: all` frees everything); an Upgrade frees the target Deck's own rows. Build reports contention it declined.
- Freshness: the brief asks once, using the newest `Added` timestamp (plus the Oracle's staleness signals); downstream stages trust their input silently.
- Condition, Language, and Foil vocabularies are treated as open behind defensive normalization (confirmed values are snake_case; Chinese language codes and `etched` remain unverified).

### Formats

- v1 Formats, all equal citizens: **Commander**, **Kitchen 20**, **Casual 60**, and thin sanctioned **Standard / Modern / Pioneer** (legality read from the Oracle's per-card legalities; no hand-maintained banlists). The four 60-card Formats share one set of review standards.
- A Format is a first-class data profile: deck size, copy limits, color rules, banlist parameters, check targets (lands, curve shape, quota numbers, consistency thresholds), per-Format review standards, and judgment-flavored lists such as which keywords count as evergreen. A later format is a new profile, not engine work.
- Kitchen 20 profile (pinned by the Foundations Beginner Box research): 20-card mono-color Pack, strict singleton nonlands, 8–9 lands with Uncharted Haven the only nonbasic, exactly 1 rare, evergreen keywords only, no multicolor cards; two Packs shuffle into a 40-card game (~16–18 lands); pack-combining quality is review guidance; the Format carries no Power.
- Play variants (Archenemy, Two-Headed Giant, Jumpstart 40) shape the Brief; the Deck is always built to some Format. The Centerpiece unifies the commander and the Archenemy villain's planeswalker.

### Blocks

- Recognition is semantic — no sentinel lines, no fence-tag reliance, no version markers. Shape alone identifies each Block; partial pastes degrade gracefully. Blocks are atomic: nothing embeds another Block. Closing instructions name which Blocks the next stage needs.
- **Deck Block** — ManaBox-importable text (owner-verified: ManaBox accepts `//` comments and reserves the four Board headers). First line `// `; Board headers `// Commander`, `// Mainboard`, `// Sideboard`, `// Maybeboard`, only the Boards the Format uses; nonbasics as pinned English lines with set code and collector number (fancier owned print wins), optional inline `// category` comments; basics lumped per name, last in each Board after a blank line; Maybeboard entries may be unowned and carry no printing pin. From the Block-formats decision:

  ```
  // Golgari Reanimator

  // Commander
  1 Meren of Clan Nel Toth (C15) 49

  // Mainboard
  1 Sol Ring (C21) 263 // ramp
  1 Eternal Witness (MH2) 302 // recursion

  12 Forest
  8 Swamp

  // Maybeboard
  1 Mikaeus, the Unhallowed // would make the deck imba
  ```

- **Brief Block** — flat `key: value` lines. Canonical keys: `name`, `format`, `centerpiece`, `identity`, `play variant`, `power`, `constraint` (repeatable), `donor` (repeatable; `donor: all` frees the whole Collection), `notes`. Only `format` is required. There is no `budget:` key.
- **Review Block** — `deck:` and `date:` reference lines, one overall `verdict:` line, then one section per axis (Standards, Brief) with its own verdict and Findings naming cards.
- **Suite report Block** — flat `suite:`/`deck:`/`format:`/`date:`/`oracle:` head, one `verdict:` line, then one `red|green  — evidence` line per Check, findings naming cards (shape from the suite prototype).
- **Table Brief Block** — same flat grammar, recognized by its `table:` anchor plus `seat:` lines; an index that never embeds the per-Deck Briefs. Seat grammar `seat: [role —] [, power N]`; the deck name joins to that Brief's `name:`. From the Tables decision:

  ```
  table: Family Archenemy Night
  format: commander
  play variant: archenemy
  power: 3
  seat: villain — Nicol Bolas, God-Pharaoh, power 4
  seat: hero — Meren Reanimator
  ```

- **Table Review Block** — `table:`/`date:` lines, one overall `verdict:`, per-axis sections whose findings name Seats and cards.

### Checks and the Suite

- A deck test is a Suite of deterministic, binary Checks generated test-first from Brief + Format profile at Build start (ADR 0003). Check classes: Legality (Format-parameterized, including Kitchen 20's packet rules and the Commander bracket's Game Changers count), Availability (owned copies, contention-aware), Mana base, Curve, Quotas (counts over Role tags), mechanical Brief constraints, and hypergeometric Consistency where the profile sets a threshold. No budget class.
- Empty-Deck semantics (ADR 0005 amending 0003): every size, mana-base, curve, and quota Check starts red; constraint-shaped Checks (singleton, legality lists, availability) may pass vacuously. Vacuous green is honest.
- Verdicts are strictly binary — no warn tier. Build may end red with an honest report; the human decides among loosening the Brief, accepting as-is, or acquiring cards.
- The Suite is declarative data interpreted by a fixed runner (ADR 0005): sections for profile targets (snapshotted at generation), quotas, mechanical constraints, and Role tags (judgment recorded once per card), plus check ids resolving to fixed predicates. The runner is a stdlib-only skill asset with its own small YAML-subset parser; the same data renders as a walkable checklist, flagged best-effort, where no sandbox exists. An Upgrade re-runs the byte-identical Suite; only cards new to the pool need fresh tagging. Portability was proven with two independent interpreters (Python and JavaScript) agreeing on every verdict — from the prototype, which is the reference implementation.
- The global Role vocabulary: ramp, draw, removal, wipe, wincon, land, theme/other. A card may carry several Roles and counts toward each; tagging is judgment, counting is mechanical.
- The Game Changers Check reads the Oracle's `game_changer` flag; bracket limits (0 / 0 / ≤3 / unlimited / unlimited for Power 1–5) are Format-profile data.

### Review

- Two axes, mirroring `/code-review` (ADR 0006): **Standards** — a format-agnostic Smell baseline plus per-Format standards, where the profile overrides the baseline — and **Brief** — fidelity to intent. No third axis.
- Smell baseline v1 (names locked, wording polished at implementation): synergy island, dead card, win-more, no comeback plan, piloting overload, fragile mana, theme tax, redundancy gap, curve lie, interaction mismatch.
- Per-Format standards are authored at implementation from recorded seeds: Kitchen 20 — Pack-combining quality, teaching pilotability, rare-as-payoff; Commander — politics, functional-copy redundancy, answer spread; one shared list for the four 60-card Formats. Power fit ("does it play like its number"), mass land denial, chained extra turns, and early two-card combos are Review judgment, not Checks.
- A Finding: severity (blocker / note) + named cards + the problem + at most one suggestion (owned swap or unowned Maybeboard candidate). Cap five per axis, worst first, plus a one-line summary of the rest. Review never edits the Deck.
- Verdicts are arithmetic: axis with any blocker → `rebuild`; only notes → `playable`; clean → `ship`; overall = worst axis. Review trusts the green Suite — it never recounts — but may flag a Check target as mis-set for the Brief.
- No Brief present: Standards-only review; the Brief axis reports "no Brief available". Closing instructions are Verdict-dependent (ship → ManaBox import suggestion; playable/rebuild → offer a Build re-run consuming the Review Block).

### The Oracle

- `/tutor:oracle` reads the Export, batch-resolves unique Scryfall IDs via Scryfall's collection endpoint (75 identifiers per call, 2 calls/second, mandatory User-Agent and Accept headers), falling back to Name + Set code for migrated or deleted IDs, and writes `oracle.jsonl` beside the Export. The bulk-file path was rejected (print-level IDs miss in the oracle-level bulk file; the download buys nothing at collection scale).
- Shape: one JSON line per unique card name — prints deduped, token rows excluded, basic lands included, multi-faced cards flattened with `//`. Fields: name, mana value, colors, color identity, type line, oracle text, legalities trimmed to standard/pioneer/modern/commander, and the `game_changer` boolean. No UUIDs.
- Line one records `generated_at` plus the source Export's newest `Added`. Two staleness signals — Export newer than the Oracle's watermark, or `generated_at` older than ~30 days — fold into the brief's single freshness question. No automation; regenerate when the Export refreshes or the nudge fires.
- A Deck card missing from the Oracle degrades per-card to flagged model knowledge; the Build report lists uncovered cards and recommends regeneration. When no Oracle exists and network allows, build offers to generate one on the spot.

### Tables

- One brief conversation per Table produces one Table Brief plus N untouched per-Deck Briefs (two Seats minimum). Table-level power, constraints, play variant, and donors copy into each Seat's Brief, so every build session reads only its own Brief.
- Seat order = build order = contention priority. Builds run sequentially through the unchanged build skill; a table-mate's finished Deck Block counts as committed copies. Table-mates are never Donor Decks; reallocation is a human loop — Table Review flags it, the owner re-briefs, affected Seats re-run in order.
- Table `power:` is inherited per Seat with per-seat override (e.g. villain above heroes); declared-power match is a mechanical Check, felt fairness is Table Review judgment. Kitchen 20 Seats carry no Power.
- One Format per Table; play variants ride on top. A Kitchen 20 Pack set built to combine is a Table like any other. Upgrading one Seat later is an ordinary Upgrade carrying the Table Brief and table-mate Deck Blocks.

### Constraint vocabulary

- `power:` is a number 1–5; free text may trail for feel ("3, battlecruiser feel") but the number is canonical. Commander reads it as the official WotC Bracket; the 60-card Formats profile-interpret it (1 jank … 5 competitive); absent defaults to 2; Kitchen 20 carries none.
- Proxies are out of scope by premise (collection-only; the Maybeboard is the valve). Budget is out entirely — no key, no price semantics.

### Versioning and release

- One release channel: the marketplace plugin (ADR 0004). One explicit semver pinned in the plugin manifest as sole version authority, mirrored into each skill's free-form metadata version — plugin and skills version in lockstep as one organism.
- A release is the deliberate version-bump commit, performed by a release script: bump, mirror into skills, draft the changelog entry (Keep a Changelog shape), run the plugin validator, tag `tutor--v{version}`, push. Unbumped merges deliberately ship nothing.
- Semver for prompt-ware: MAJOR = existing artifacts break (a Block format change an existing Block cannot survive through Upgrade, or a skill/command removed or renamed); MINOR = new capability (Format profile, skill, Check class); PATCH = prompt fixes, wording, docs inside skills.
- README documents the update path (auto-update off by default for self-hosted marketplaces). No stable/latest split; GitHub Releases deferred until the public phase.

### Legal

- tutor is unofficial Fan Content under the WotC Fan Content Policy. The mandated disclaimer ships verbatim: "tutor is unofficial Fan Content permitted under the Fan Content Policy. Not approved/endorsed by Wizards. Portions of the materials used are property of Wizards of the Coast. ©Wizards of the Coast LLC."
- Scryfall notices apply (tutor calls the Scryfall API in the oracle skill): no implied endorsement, price/legality data marked informational-only, artist/copyright credit preserved if card images are ever rendered.
- Placements: a Legal section in the README, a canonical NOTICE file at the repo root carrying the full composite text, the short form in the plugin and marketplace descriptions, and a short-form footer line on generated deck artifacts plus a price/legality caveat wherever those surface. The plugin stays free and unpaywalled — a condition of both policies.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test**: judge external behavior only. A skill is judged by the artifacts and transcript it produces — the Blocks emitted, the Checks run, the files written — never by its internal reasoning. A Check is judged by its verdict over a given Deck and Oracle. Planted flaws in fixtures make judgment measurable.
- **Seams** (existing ones, at the highest point; no new seams proposed): the **skill boundary** — files/Blocks in, files/Blocks out — is where Evals drive brief, build, review, and oracle end-to-end; and the **Suite runner** — the one deterministic code seam, running offline over Suite + Deck + Oracle files. Deck-test Checks are the single authority on deck correctness; Eval graders wrap the runner rather than re-implement legality logic.
- **Harness, staged**: the plugin validator's strict mode runs in CI on every PR from day one; the skill-creator eval workflow is the dev-time behavioral harness; the gated `claude plugin eval` becomes the CI behavioral gate when org enablement lands (cases authored in skill-creator format now, ported then — its grader vocabulary maps cleanly onto the loop).
- **Depth split**: deep behavioral Evals for build and review; smoke for brief (fires from natural language, valid Brief Block from scripted answers) and for oracle (against the pinned snapshot). Brief conversation quality stays human-judged.
- **Input modes**: file-on-disk is primary; one pasted-Export case remains as parser-tolerance smoke.
- **Graders, two tiers**: hard mechanical invariants — every Deck card drawn from the Collection fixture, Format legality, the Deck Block parses as ManaBox-importable text, Blocks survive the round-trip — any failure red; soft LLM judgment — the Deck honors the Brief's intent, the Review catches planted flaws. Baseline/ablation grading joins for regression once plugin eval is available.
- **Fixtures, four kinds**: the real captured export (577 rows, ManaBox 4.1.12) as the realism fixture; small synthetic Collections for what it lacks (etched foil, non-English languages, promo collector numbers, per-Format shaped pools); fixture Briefs and Decks, some with planted flaws; and a pinned Scryfall snapshot covering only fixture cards, committed beside them and refreshed deliberately. **Evals never call the live API** — runs stay deterministic and offline.
- **Prior art**: the suite-shape prototype — fixture Suite, two independent interpreters, three-stage captured runs (empty / planted-violations draft / green final) — is the model for Check-level testing; the skill-creator eval workflow is the model for skill-level Evals.

## Out of Scope

- **Building unowned-card decks, proxies, and budget reasoning** — tutor builds from the Collection; the Maybeboard is the only home for unowned cards; no price semantics anywhere.
- **The claude.ai chat runtime and skill-ZIP channel** — retired (ADR 0004, ADR 0007). Reviving chat is a fresh effort.
- **Goldfishing and turn simulation** — only closed-form hypergeometric math qualifies as a Check; whether any simulation ever joins Review is a later question.
- **Scheme decks** — fixed product, no construction choice; a Brief may note the villain's table role.
- **Mixed-Format Tables** — one Format per Table until a real sitting demands otherwise.
- **An automatic review→build loop** — the human reads the Review and re-runs Build; some findings are taste.
- **Automatic seat reallocation** — contention across a Table resolves through a human re-brief, never by unbuilding an earlier Seat.
- **Release channels, GitHub Releases, and public distribution** — one marketplace, one channel, main is it; the public phase ("the world next") is a later effort.
- **Collection compaction** — the raw CSV is read whole; revisit only near ~2,000 rows.
- **Card acquisition advice** — Build may state that acquiring cards is an option when ending red; recommending purchases is not tutor's job.

## Further Notes

- **Provenance**: this spec assembles the decisions of the wayfinder map [Wayfinder map: tutor — MTG deckbuilding plugin with its own marketplace](https://github.com/mattiasthalen/tutor/issues/2) — every closed child ticket's resolution comment is source material. ADRs 0001–0007 and the `CONTEXT.md` glossary are binding; where this spec and an ADR diverge, flag it rather than silently overriding.
- **Reference assets**: the suite-shape prototype (runnable Suite, two interpreters, captured runs, interactive demo) lives on branch `claude/deck-test-artifact-shape-wk1txl`; the real export sample and verification script on `claude/manabox-export-sample-irxrfp`; research write-ups on their `research/*` branches, linked from each research ticket.
- **Open verifications, parser posture only**: Chinese language codes and the `etched` foil value remain unobserved in a real export; both touch ignored or normalized columns, so they gate nothing — keep the vocabularies open behind defensive normalization.
- **Kitchen 20 life total** (20) is medium-confidence — the printed booklet was never inspected; nothing mechanical depends on it.
- **Plugin eval enablement** is org-gated and publicly undocumented; spike it at implementation time rather than blocking on it.
- **The deck library vision**: the owner's Collection home accumulates many built Decks and Tables — "generate MANY decks and tables… look it up and build the decks when I want." Skills should treat the `decks/` folder as a growing library, not a scratch directory.
- **Posture**: me first, the world next. The repo is private today; the legal wording is already public-ready; whether the real collection sample ships publicly parks with the release flow when the public phase arrives.

Hand the axes a layer-attribution map (ticket → PR) so every finding routes to the PR of the layer that owns it, and cross-layer findings to the parent issue. Disclose which children are parked or red before the Spec axis runs, so their absent work is not misread as gaps in the parent's coverage. Findings are REPORTED, never fixed — a fix in layer N forces a rebase of every layer above it. Routing after the report: a runtime bug worth fixing pre-merge becomes one new ticket plus one new top layer closing it (no mid-stack rework); cosmetic and structural debt becomes grouped tickets (here: https://github.com/mattiasthalen/tutor/issues/75 and https://github.com/mattiasthalen/tutor/issues/76); already-ruled per-layer deviations are reported as "known, ruled", never rediscovered.

Because that was the deal we struck: you picked "fix layer for the bug + tickets for the rest", and I scoped #75/#76 as post-merge debt on purpose — none of it fires at runtime, and every extra pre-merge layer adds review surface to a stack you have not started merging. Bug blocked release; wording and dedup did not. So they became tickets, not layers.

But half of them are cheap enough to do now if you want the stack to land fully clean:

1. **#75 whole** (manifest key, avoid-term, hello line, CI label) — one small layer 15, ~zero risk, expectation-registry sync is the only careful part.
2. **#76 partial** (shared test helper, width unification) — mechanical; the `run_evals.py` split stays deferred by its own finding ("at the next growth spurt"), and the fixture-Role quirk stays a note.

Say which — both, #75 only, or leave as tickets — and it happens. Question.

content.text:
No ticket needed — you thought right, and both things are true at once:

**Pointing at the repo IS the distribution.** `/plugin marketplace add mattiasthalen/tutor` reads `marketplace.json` off `main`; a fresh install pulls whatever `main` holds at that moment. Merge the stack and the plugin is live for any new install. No build, no publish, no CD pipeline exists to set up.

**The version bump is for *existing* installs.** `/plugin update tutor` compares versions — manifest still says 0.1.0 after your merge, so the updater answers "already at the latest version" and changes nothing (#50's tests prove exactly this message). That is ADR 0004 on purpose: "unbumped merges deliberately ship nothing" — release is a human act, not a side effect of merging. `scripts/release minor` (or whatever bump you judge) is your whole CD: bump, mirror into skills, changelog, validate, tag, push — one command from any session in the repo.

So the flow after merge: nothing more if you reinstall fresh on your devices; or run `scripts/release` once and `/plugin update tutor` everywhere picks it up. Automating release-on-merge would be a ticket — but it would also contradict ADR 0004's deliberate-release rule, so that is an ADR amendment conversation first, not a backlog item to slip in. My take: keep it manual, it is one command and the whole point of the design.

content.content:
# Pull Request Merge Endpoints

## Synchronous Merge
**HTTP Method:** PUT
**Path:** `"/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge"`
**Body Parameters:**
- `commit_title` (string)
- `commit_message` (string)
- `sha` (string)
- `merge_method` (string): one of `merge`, `squash`, `rebase`

## Asynchronous Merge
**HTTP Method:** PUT
**Path:** `"/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge-async"`
**Body Parameters:**
- `commit_title` (string)
- `commit_message` (string)
- `sha` (string)
- `merge_method` (string): one of `merge`, `squash`, `rebase`
- `merge_action` (string): one of `default`, `direct_merge`, `merge_queue`

## Get Asynchronous Merge Result
**HTTP Method:** GET
**Path:** `"/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/merge-async/{uuid}"`
**Body Parameters:** None

The documentation indicates the async endpoint supports stacked pull request merging and merge queue operations through the `merge_action` parameter.

input.title: Optimize the /swarm orchestrator to stay in the smartzone
input.body:
## Problem

The swarm orchestrator's own context grows monotonically across a run, and judgment quality degrades with depth. Evidence from the tutor v1 run (mattiasthalen/tutor#46 — 13 tickets, 14 stacked layers, ~40 subagents, whole-stack post-review, merge):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator turns | 700 |
| Context at first turn | 45,707 tokens |
| Context at last turn | 594,011 tokens |
| Median / mean context | 305,733 / 311,790 |
| Turns under 200k ("smartzone") | 215 (31%) |
| Turns above 400k | 254 (36%) |
| Turns above 500k | 100 (14%) |
| Orchestrator output total | 740,361 tokens |

The run stayed correct to the end, but two-thirds of all orchestrator decisions — including every late-stack rebase-conflict resolution and the whole-stack review routing — were made above 300k. The deepest work (the #58/#59 rebases, where a botched union produced Python chimera functions that needed hand surgery) landed exactly in the deepest context.

## Where the tokens went (observed, in rough order of weight)

1. **Whole ticket/PR bodies fetched inline.** The parent spec (#46) alone is ~15k tokens and was fetched into the orchestrator once; every child ticket body was fetched inline before dispatch and again for review prompts; every PR body was re-fetched whole to re-save it (the sidebar-link workaround) and to patch stale sentences.
2. **Per-turn system-reminder repetition.** The full skills listing (~4k tokens) was injected into the orchestrator dozens of times; task-list reminders repeated the same 14 lines at high frequency.
3. **Subagent completion reports.** Implementer reports ran long (one-paragraph rule held, but paragraphs of 300–400 words × ~40 agents); review reports were capped at 400–500 words, which worked well.
4. **Inline mechanical work.** Rebase conflict resolution (reading conflicted hunks, splicing functions), stack API probing, and evals.json case-renumbering were all done in the orchestrator's own context because they touch the shared worktrees between agent lifetimes.

## Candidate optimizations (for grilling, not settled)

- **Fetch tickets filtered.** Dispatch needs title + acceptance criteria + blocked-by, not the whole body; review prompts could carry the criteria the orchestrator already holds instead of re-fetching. A one-call "criteria extract" via a cheap subagent would keep whole bodies out of the orchestrator entirely.
- **Stop re-fetching PR bodies.** The orchestrator authors or receives every body once; hold a body cache (or write bodies to files at creation) so the link-nudge re-save and stale-sentence patches never round-trip the full text through context again.
- **Delegate the rebase step.** Layer-stacking rebases are the heaviest inline work and they always happen late (deep context).
